summary.zh: 蜂蜜色的松软饼皮夹着绵密红豆沙，哆啦A梦最爱的国民点心。
summary.en: Honey-gold fluffy pancakes sandwiching sweet red bean paste — the national snack beloved by Doraemon.

ingredients.zh: 水或牛奶 1–2 大勺（调稠度）

steps.zh: 鸡蛋加细砂糖打发至颜色发白、体积略膨。
steps.en: Beat the eggs with sugar until pale and slightly voluminous.

steps.zh: 加蜂蜜拌匀，筛入面粉和泡打粉，翻拌成顺滑面糊，太稠加 1–2 大勺水。
steps.en: Mix in honey, sift in flour and baking powder, fold into a smooth batter — loosen with water if too thick.

steps.zh: 盖保鲜膜醒 15 分钟，让泡打粉起效、面糊更细腻。
steps.en: Rest the batter 15 minutes under wrap so the baking powder activates.

steps.zh: 平底锅最小火，舀一勺面糊从高处落下自然摊成 8 厘米圆饼。
steps.en: Over the lowest heat, drop a ladle of batter from a height — it spreads into an 8cm round on its own.

steps.zh: 表面冒出密集小泡、边缘微干时翻面，再煎 30 秒。
steps.en: When bubbles cover the surface and edges look dry, flip; 30 seconds more.

steps.zh: 两片饼中间夹 1 大勺红豆沙，轻压边缘合拢即成。
steps.en: Sandwich a spoonful of red bean paste between two pancakes and press the edges gently.

tips.zh: 全程最小火，才能煎出均匀漂亮的蜂蜜色，火大必花脸。
tips.en: Lowest heat throughout — that's the only way to an even honey-brown face; higher heat scorches it blotchy.

tips.zh: 面糊稠度以「滴落成圆」为准，太稠饼厚，太稀不成形。
tips.en: Batter consistency test: it should drop and settle into a round — thicker means dense cakes, thinner means shapeless.

tips.zh: 夹馅时边缘留 1 厘米，轻压后豆沙刚好铺满不外溢。
tips.en: Leave a 1cm border when filling — a gentle press spreads the paste exactly to the edge.

failChecks.zh: 上色不均或焦黑：火太大或锅太热，煎几片后让锅离火降温。
failChecks.en: Blotchy or burnt? The pan got too hot — lift it off the flame between batches.

failChecks.zh: 饼不松软：没加泡打粉或没醒面，15 分钟不能省。
failChecks.en: Dense pancakes? You skipped the baking powder or the rest — 15 minutes is non-negotiable.

failChecks.zh: 豆沙挤出来：馅放太多，1 大勺配 8 厘米饼刚好。
failChecks.en: Filling squirting out? Too much paste — one tablespoon per 8cm cake is just right.

culturalStory.zh: 传说平安时代，武士源义经受伤时受僧人铜锣款待，临别以铜锣相赠，僧人用锣烙饼——铜锣烧由此得名（虽是附会但足够可爱）。现代两片夹豆沙的形态诞生于 1914 年东京上野「うさぎや」。当然，让它走向世界的，是那只最爱铜锣烧的蓝色机器猫哆啦A梦。
culturalStory.en: Legend says the wounded warrior Minamoto no Yoshitsune was sheltered by a monk and gave him a gong (dora) in thanks — the monk baked cakes on it, naming the dorayaki. The modern two-pancake form was born in 1914 at Usagiya in Tokyo's Ueno. But it was a blue robot cat from the 22nd century — Doraemon — who made the dorayaki world-famous.
